topics.title: Reasons Why We Pray Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES
RELIGION AND NATIONAL VALUES
FIRST TERM
WEEK 2
PRIMARY 2
THEME - PRAYER
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning of Prayer Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - REASONS WHY WE PRAY
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Reasons Why We Pray
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain the meaning of prayer.
2. give reasons why we pray.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can say Lord’s Prayer correctly.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Written prayers (The Lord’s Prayer).
2. Pictures showing people in prayer.
3. Bible Reading - Matthew 7:7 - 11
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Prayer is a way we talk to God and God talks to us.
People pray for so many things. People prayers are different from one another depending on their needs and wants. Some of the reasons we pray are -
REASONS WHY WE PRAY
1. We pray for good health.
2. We pray for Protection.
3. We pray for wealth (money).
4. We pray for promotion.
5. We pray for journey mercy, etc.
LESSON 2 - REVISION AND WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Leads pupils to say the Lord’s Prayer correctly.
Pupil’s Activities - Say the Lord’s Prayer correctly.
3. Discuss the meaning of prayer.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in discussion on prayer.
4. Helps pupils to understand and state why people pray.
Pupil’s Activities - State the reasons why people pray.
5. Summarizes each of the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. say the Lord’s prayer.
2. Say the meaning of prayer.
WORKBOOK
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
1. ______ is a way we talk to God and God talks to us.
A. Prayer
B. Talk
2. When pray we pray to ______.
A. God
B. Ourselves
3. We must pray everyday.
A. Yes
B. No
4. When we were pray, we talk to God.
A. Yes
B. Not
5. Everybody pray.
A. Yes
No
6. We must always pray for our family.
A. Yes
B. No
7. We must pray for Nigeria too.
A. Yes
B. No
8. When we pray, we ask God for our daily needs.
A. Yes
B. No
9. Pray is the master key.
A. Yes
B. No
10. Jesus also pray.
A. Yes
B. No
11. Jesus started with _______.
A. Pray
B. Talk
12. Jesus ended with _______.
A. Pray
B. Talk
13. We can pray any where.
A. Yes
B. No
14. Do you pray before you eat?
A. Yes
B. No
15. Do you pray today?
A. Yes
No

topics.title: Right Attitude to Prayer Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES
RELIGION AND NATIONAL VALUES
FIRST TERM
WEEK 4
PRIMARY 2
THEME - PRAYER
PREVIOUS LESSON - The Lord’s Prayer (Primary 2)
TOPIC - MEANING OF PRAYER
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Right Attitude to Prayer
2. Drama
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives - state the right to prayer.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can say Lord’s Prayer
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Written prayers (The Lord’s Prayer).
2. Pictures showing people in prayer.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
The Lord’s Prayer (Primary 2)
RIGHT ATTITUDE TO PRAYER
1. We must not be boastful.
2. We must not look down on other people.
3. We must be humble.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Tells the story of the Pharisees and Tax collector.
Pupil’s Activities - Listen to the story.
3. Discuss the moral lesson of story.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the class discussion.
4. Organizes a short drama based on the story of Pharisees and Tax collector.
Pupil’s Activities - Dramatize the right attitude to prayer.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - Jesus Teaching on How to Pray (Primary 2)
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. state 3 attitude to prayer.
2. dramatize right right attitude to prayer.
